svg.text: PatchTST - architecture and the shape of the data at every layer
Nie et al., ICLR 2023 · every glyph on the left is the real array at that stage of a forward pass · M = 7, L = 336, P = 16, S = 8, N = 42, D = 128, T = 96
x̃ = (x − μ) / σ · per instance, per channel
μ, σ kept for the output
window P = 16, stride S = 8, pad S copies of xL
one direct multi-step forecast, no decoder
× σ, + μ, then stack the M channels
one N×N map per head, per channel
patches non-overlapping (P = S = 12), 40% set to zero
a masked patch cannot be interpolated from its
neighbours - the model must learn global structure
reconstruct the masked patches, MSE loss
The two ideas, in one line each:
Patching - a token is a subseries of P steps, so N ≈ L/S tokens instead of L: attention costs O(N²) ≈ O(L²/S²), a 64× cut at S = 8.
Channel-independence - the M series pass through one shared backbone as separate samples (a reshape B×M×P×N → (B·M)×P×N), so nothing is mixed across channels.
